questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Australia have been a dream for me to visit and live in for many years now, im so grateful to get the chance to live that dream through going on exchange

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. I found Griffith university was very welcoming an helping with answering questions and letting know where to direct certain questions to.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I signed up to next to everything in the Orientation week, where all the possibilities for assistance was walked through more than once

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found the housing through Griffith university's website under their recommendations. I do not recommend this. The place I stay I found did not live up to the pictures or features promised and they where at such over expensive as what they offered.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Wait to find a place till you are here and can go and see the place.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Additional help with finding housing would have been nice

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: pretty easy, help easily assessable

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Buddy program with fellow students, International counselers

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes I signed up for

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: search out where you can get help so you know where to go before you need the help

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didnt find the academic level as good as my home institution

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: i had fully electives and chose courses outside of my program at home, and from what I heard from fellow students the level was more likely at a bachelors level in europe at the masters here

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I especially loved the teaching of one of my professors, who very much applied the teachings so that we understood how to apply it in real life, in stead of the most that sticks to theory. I did had another one who, by my opinion should not be a teacher, just as smart and succesful as I am sure she is, she just don't know how to engage that in order for students to learn and gain interest.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
GLOBALISATION AND CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY 7112IBA
CORPORATE ENTREPRENEURSHIP AND CHANGE 7128IBA
POLICY AND ORGANISATIONAL CHANGE 7012EHR
GLOBAL BUSINESS STRATEGY 7008IBA

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
CORPORATE ENTREPRENEURSHIP AND CHANGE 7128IBA
Maybe the best professor that I have had in my entire masters program. This is also a course that I think anyone whould benefit from taking.

questions.answer: Just the expense of living, much more expensive than anticipated

questions.answer: Housing, food, experiences

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not very many og very interesting opportunities for social activities. But it was possible to attend UQ's activities which where very good.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: not sure as there wasn't many

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go exploring as much as possible on weekends, there is a lot of beautiful places around Brisbane perfect for a weekend away.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Stratbroke island, Moreton Island, Gold Coast, Sunshine Coast, Springbok national park, Hinterland of Gold Coast, Hinterland of Sunshine Coast, Everglades in the Sunshine Coast

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very, but I did my homework before coming too. Not a culture shock.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No, I mostly meet international to al the events. It's hard to meet locals. Maybe if you got a job, or private housing share house with locals

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their openness, kindness, laidback attitude, the mindset of "no worries"

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Stay in the city of Brisbane instead of close to campus - there is noting else to mention out there. 
Attend as much as you can during Orientation week - this is where you will meet the majority of people you will spend you time with.
Ask a lot of questions, about anything, to anyone. Everyone is very helpful

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: none that I haven't already mentioned

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To emerge myself in a new culture, meet new people

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Housing

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
